movement_profile.arms_and_hands: free improvisation representing a playful indigenous wooing game
movement_profile.footwork: rapid heel-and-toe stamps, foot glides (glissements de pied), and in later French periods, cabrioles and battus
movement_profile.formation_and_space: single couple facing each other, or two opposing rows approaching and retreating
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: energetic and violent movement contrasting standard court stiffness
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: frequent low stamps transitioning into high aerial cabrioles in the Baroque era
movement_profile.partnering: a fiery wooing dialogue between partners with free improvisational sections
movement_profile.posture: upright courtly carriage combined with vigorous, low-level bending for stamps and jumps

signature_moves.description: Rapid striking of the floor with heel and toe on the first beat of the measure.
signature_moves.name: heel-and-toe stamp

signature_moves.description: High-energy vertical jumps with violent leg action.
signature_moves.name: frogs legs jump

movement_profile.tempo_feel: extremely fast, endiablée (endless/wild), sharper and quicker than a gigue

music_profile.musical_form: instrumental suite section, balletto sequence, or ostinato variations

reference_recordings.title: Instrucción de Música sobre la Guitarra Española (Canarios)

music_profile.rhythm_pattern: dotted notes with an upbeat (anacrusis) consisting of a sixteenth and eighth, or eighth and quarter
music_profile.sound_description: A rapid, driving instrumental movement driven by sharp, short bow strokes or plucked strings, defined by an energetic dotted rhythm and an insistent repeating melodic or bass cell.

basic_steps: cabrioles and battus (in later French form)
teaching.formation: most often choreographed for a single couple; two rows of dancers in traditional accounts
teaching.level_notes: Early Renaissance forms permitted free improvisation of stamps and jumps; later Baroque forms required advanced technique including rapid bowing, cabrioles, and turns.
teaching.rhythm: syncopated rhythms, dotted 3/4 or 6/8 meter, or early allabreve
